# Hardware Readiness Checklist: Cryptographic Architecture and phyco-v3 Design

**Purpose**: Unit tests for the requirements that prepare `phyco-v3` for RTL and the board: carry
chains per stage, constant time, zeroization, grid generics, the width, signedness and shift kind
of every operation, FUT-GRID-1 to FUT-GRID-5 and FUT-HW-1 to FUT-HW-5.
**Created**: 2026-11-01
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), with [plan.md](../plan.md) and [research.md](../research.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Carry chains, pipeline stages and throughput

- [x] CHK001 Is FR-025's "at most one or two serial 32-bit carry chains" resolved to one number
  per pipeline stage (research R5 reads it as at most 2), with the timing argument for it at the
  XC7A100T's −1 speed grade and 200 MHz, and is it stated whether a subtraction, or the increment
  of a public counter held as 32-bit words with a carry rule, counts as a chain? [Ambiguity,
  Spec §FR-025, §Re-decided feature-002 requirements "FR-002"; research R5; FUT-HW-2]
- [x] CHK002 Is a limit or an estimate stated for the LUT levels on a stage's path besides its
  carry chains, for example a bitwise function with more than six inputs per output bit, which
  research R5 counts as ⌈(k − 1)/5⌉ LUTs per bit, so that the 200 MHz target is designed for and
  not only the chain count? [Gap, Spec §FR-025; research R5; FUT-HW-2]
- [x] CHK003 Is the clock-cycle unit consistent, given that research R5's cost per output bit and
  implied throughput assume one round per clock cycle while R11 makes each colour phase a pipeline
  stage, so that a two- or three-colour round takes two or three cycles unless its phases share
  one stage, which puts more carry chains on one path? [Conflict, Spec §FR-025, §FR-026;
  research R5, R11]
- [x] CHK004 Is it stated that the 2w-bit ARX-box of FR-022 is built from w-bit operations only,
  as the re-decided FR-002 keeps every datapath word at 32 bits, and how FR-025's "32-bit" chains
  read at the reduced widths 4, 8 and 16? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-025, §Re-decided
  feature-002 requirements "FR-002"]
- [x] CHK005 Is the width of the output interface stated per size, and is FR-026's implied
  throughput required to be the lesser of r/R bits per cycle and what that interface carries,
  given that r/R at 16×16, where r = 16,128 bits, is far above 32 bits per cycle? [Clarity,
  Spec §FR-026; research R5; data-model §10; FUT-HW-3]
- [x] CHK006 Is FR-026's implied throughput required to include the forget call after every
  request and the cost of instantiate, for a stated request size, given that research R5 quotes
  its rates "before forget calls"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, §FR-013; research R5]
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec require an estimate, from the cost model, of which claimable sizes are
  expected to fit the XC7A100T-1 (63,400 LUTs, 126,800 flip-flops, 0 DSP blocks), so that
  FUT-HW-2's "largest supported grid that fits" is anticipated before feature 008 measures it?
  [Gap, Spec §FR-026; FUT-HW-2; seed-entropy note §5.2]
- [x] CHK008 Are the absorption and output trees specified per size (fan-in per stage, depth,
  registered stages, latency), with that latency included in FR-025's latency to the first output
  and in FR-026's throughput, and is the timing justification the plan promises for them required
  as a stated argument? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, §FR-025, §FR-026; plan "Complexity
  Tracking"; constitution Principle III]
- [x] CHK009 Is a timing justification required for the round and phase counters and the reset,
  which research R15 makes global, as Principle III requires of "global broadcast signals across
  the grid", given that the plan names the absorption and output trees as Principle III's only
  exception? [Conflict, constitution Principle III; research R15; plan "Complexity Tracking"]

## Constant time

- [x] CHK010 Do the re-decided FR-001 ("no table lookup, comparison or selection on secret data")
  and the model contract's `KeyMismatch`, which compares the key of each instantiate with the bound
  key, agree? If the check stays, are the retention of the bound key, its zeroization and a
  constant-time comparison specified? [Conflict, Spec §Re-decided feature-002 requirements
  "FR-001", §FR-020; model contract "Generator"]
- [x] CHK011 Is it stated which input lengths are public (the personalization string, the reseed
  input, the request size), so that a cycle count that depends on them is allowed under FR-020,
  and is the reseed input's length public even when the input itself is secret? [Clarity,
  Spec §FR-020, §FR-013, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK012 Is "constant time" defined for each implementation, as a fixed cycle count in
  hardware, as no secret-dependent branch or memory index in feature 006's C implementation, and
  as branch-free only in the Python model, whose integers are not constant time, so that no
  artifact calls the model constant time? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020; research R17]
- [x] CHK013 Is the cycle count of every call stated as a function of public values only (call
  type, size, request length), including the forget after every request, a refused request and
  the start-up self-test, so that FUT-HW-5's constant-time test in feature 008 has an expected
  count to compare with? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020, §FR-025, §FR-059; FUT-HW-5]

## Zeroization, key storage and read-back

- [x] CHK014 Is "the whole state" to be zeroized enumerated (lanes, pipeline registers, the
  registers of the absorption and output trees, the key-loading buffer, any held key, the
  counters), with every trigger (reset, an explicit call, a failed self-test, a limit reached)
  and the latency of each? [Completeness, Spec §FR-025, §FR-059; FUT-HW-5]
- [x] CHK015 Is the hardware counterpart of the model's "zeroize is final" specified: whether a
  reset or a zeroization returns the device to a state that accepts a new key, and that the
  per-key limits and counters then become usage rules for the caller across resets, as the model
  contract states across objects? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025, §FR-007; model contract
  "Generator"]
- [x] CHK016 Is it specified that no output, and no output-valid signal, can follow a zeroization
  or a reset until an instantiate has completed, as the model refuses generate before
  instantiate? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025, §FR-058; model contract "Generator"]
- [x] CHK017 Is "no read-back path for key or state" defined to cover the FPGA's configuration
  readback and any inserted debug core, which feature 008 must lock (for example with the
  bitstream's readback-security setting), or only the RTL's own ports? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025;
  FUT-HW-5; security.md §13]
- [x] CHK018 Is it stated how constructed-state vectors (FR-054), which start from chosen states,
  are applied to the RTL and the board without a state-load or read-back port in production, for
  example through a simulation-only path or a separate test build, so that FR-025's "no
  read-back path" and FUT-HW-4's equivalence both hold? [Conflict, Spec §FR-025, §FR-054;
  FUT-HW-4, FUT-HW-5]
- [x] CHK019 Is the start-up self-test's scope defined (which calls it runs, and whether it passes
  every node, lane, constant ROM, both trees and the counters), and is its expected output given
  for each claimable size, since n is a generic? [Completeness, Spec §FR-059, §FR-018]
- [x] CHK020 Is T4 (timing, power, EM, fault injection) given a disposition for `phyco-v3` beyond
  constant time, with the behaviour on reset and clock glitches specified or deferred to feature
  008 with its risk stated, given that a state compromised in mid-request exposes, through Π⁻¹,
  everything back to the last forget call, which for a first request may reach the key's
  absorption unless instantiate ends with a forget? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-025; FUT-HW-5;
  security.md §5; plan "Other choices"; research R9]

## Grid generics and locality

- [x] CHK021 Is it stated whether an odd n, which needs a three-colour schedule, is the same core
  under FUT-GRID-1's "without restructuring the core", and how the generic n selects the
  schedule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, §Edge Cases "Odd grid sizes"; FUT-GRID-1; research R14]
- [x] CHK022 Is it stated how the constant tables for every n and w the generics cover reach the
  RTL (one generated package per supported size, or the rule evaluated at elaboration), given
  that research R15 keeps the LFSR only in the script and FR-018 asks for generics covering every
  n from 2 to 16? [Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-023; research R15; FUT-GRID-1, FUT-GRID-4]
- [x] CHK023 Is a "channel" defined (a w-bit link per direction, per lane or per phase), so that
  FR-018's "at most four channels per node" can be judged on each candidate's operation list,
  the local linear layer between ARX-boxes included? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, §FR-022;
  FUT-GRID-1; research R11]
- [x] CHK024 Is "joins neighbouring nodes of the layout" defined for the folded torus, where
  logical neighbours sit up to two positions apart, with the longest link stated for odd n as
  well as even? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018; strategy note §5.4]
- [x] CHK025 Are the number of food nodes per size and the depth of the ROM at each (R rounds, or
  more if the call types draw on distinct constant streams) stated, so that the constant storage
  per node can be estimated, since the cost model does not count the ROMs? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-018, §FR-023; research R5, R15]
- [x] CHK026 Is the key-loading interface required to be generic in the capacity c, since keyed
  reduced variants take a c-bit key and a c/2-bit nonce, or defined only for the 256-bit key of
  the claimable sizes, and is the choice stated against FUT-GRID-2's "defined for every supported
  size"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025; FUT-GRID-2; research R14]

## Width, signedness and shift kind of every operation

- [x] CHK027 Do FR-027 ("signedness ... of every operation") and FR-055 (only sign-free operations
  on state words) agree on what the design document writes for a sign-free operation, for example
  `unsigned` throughout, so that a translator cannot choose `signed` where a later resize or
  comparison would then extend the sign? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, §FR-055; hardware note R4]
- [x] CHK028 Is it required that every shift and rotation amount lies in 1 to w − 1 at every
  width, after the scaling rule as well, given that at w = 4 an amount can round to 0 or to w,
  and that a rotation by 0 written as two shifts shifts by w, which is undefined in C?
  [Edge Case, Spec §FR-024, §FR-027, §FR-055; research R14]
- [x] CHK029 Are the bit numbering, the index direction of a word and the direction of each
  rotation stated, since `x(0)` is the least significant bit of an `unsigned(w − 1 downto 0)` but
  the most significant bit of an `unsigned(0 to w − 1)`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027; FUT-HW-1;
  hardware note R4]
- [x] CHK030 Does FR-027's list (width, signedness, wrap rule, shift kind, comparison semantics,
  update order) cover Principle I's truncation and rounding rule, for example for the last
  output block of a request whose length is not a multiple of r, and for the padding? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-027, §FR-014; constitution Principle I]

## Interfaces and the reset sequence

- [x] CHK031 Is the flow control of the key-loading, absorption and output interfaces specified
  (valid only, or valid and ready, and what happens while the consumer stalls), and is it stated
  that a stall changes neither the output sequence nor makes any cycle count depend on secret
  data? [Gap, Spec §FR-025; FUT-HW-3, FUT-HW-4]
- [x] CHK032 Is the latency "from reset to the first output" stated in cycles from a defined event
  (reset released with the key ready, or the last key word accepted), so that it does not depend
  on the host's timing, and does it include the self-test and the zeroization after it?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, §FR-059]

## FUT-GRID-1 to FUT-GRID-5 and FUT-HW-1 to FUT-HW-5

- [x] CHK033 Is FUT-GRID-1's expected status, "Met by specification and model", consistent with
  research R14, where n = 5, 6, 7 and 9…15 have no vectors, R_f, R_b or bounds and stay open items
  against FUT-GRID-1? [Conflict, Spec §Security Policy traceability, §FR-018; research R14]
- [x] CHK034 Are the clauses the traceability table does not name given a disposition: FUT-GRID-3's
  "Output taps MUST NOT depend only on a local neighbourhood", and FUT-GRID-4's "The disruption
  behaviour MUST be re-established at each size", not applicable once D5 removes the disruption?
  [Coverage, Spec §Security Policy traceability, §FR-029, §FR-031; seed-entropy note §5.1]
- [x] CHK035 Is FUT-GRID-5's "Validate an intermediate size, for example 4×4, before 16×16"
  carried to features 006 and 008 for the RTL and the board, with research R7's order of sizes as
  its pattern? [Coverage, Spec §FR-036; research R7; seed-entropy note §5.1]
- [x] CHK036 Is each FUT-HW item this feature designs for given an acceptance criterion at the
  design level, for example 0 DSP blocks as no multiplication in the operation set (with synthesis
  still told not to map additions to DSP slices), constant time as the stated cycle counts, and no
  read-back as an enumerated list of ports, so that "Designed for" and "Specified" in the
  traceability table can be checked? [Measurability, Spec §Security Policy traceability; FUT-HW-1
  to FUT-HW-5]
- [x] CHK037 Is the trace granularity of the vectors matched to the pipeline stage, given that
  data-model §11 traces the first four Π inputs round by round while a stage is a colour phase
  (research R11), so that an RTL mismatch can be located to one stage? [Completeness,
  Spec §FR-036, §FR-056; data-model §11; research R11]

## Re-run after the checklist answers (2026-11-01)

Items found when the checklist was run again over the text changed by the answers of 2026-11-01.
They are open like every other item; the reviewer ticks them.

- [x] CHK038 Is FR-025's second latency figure, "from the last key word accepted to the first output
  valid", consistent with the split the model contract now makes (the key loaded once and held, each
  `instantiate` taking a nonce and using the stored key), or should it run from the last nonce or
  personalization word of an instantiate, with key loading a call of its own with its own cycle
  count? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025, §FR-020; model contract "Generator"]
- [x] CHK039 Is "an error path" among the hardware zeroization triggers defined, naming the
  conditions in the RTL that count as an error after the state has changed, as distinct from a
  refused request that changes nothing, given that the model's counterpart, an exception after the
  state changed, has no direct equivalent in hardware? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025 "Zeroization"; model
  contract "Failure paths"]
- [x] CHK040 Is the recovery after a failed start-up self-test specified for the device: whether a
  later reset runs the self-test again and the device may then be used if it passes, or whether the
  failure stays latched until a stated action, and whether the failure is visible on an output or
  status signal rather than only as calls refused? [Gap, Recovery; Spec §FR-059, §FR-025]
- [x] CHK041 Is the carried rule "the board validates 4×4 before 8×8 and 16×16" (FUT-GRID-5;
  security.md §22 row 5a.5) reconciled with FUT-HW-2's "at 4×4 and at the largest grid that fits",
  so that feature 008 is never required to validate a size the XC7A100T cannot hold, with FR-026's
  LUT and flip-flop estimate named as the input that decides which sizes the board takes?
  [Consistency, Spec §FR-036, §FR-056, §FR-026; security.md §20.1, §22]
- [x] CHK042 Is it specified how a stall (ready low) reaches every node and every replicated round
  and phase counter on the same cycle, for example as a clock enable through a registered fan-out
  tree with a stated latency, or by output buffering so that the core never stalls in mid-call,
  given that the counters run in lockstep and no counter value crosses the grid? [Gap, Spec §FR-025
  "Flow control", "Key loading and reset"; plan Complexity Tracking]

## Notes

- Generated on 2026-11-01, after plan approval, from the hardware-readiness focus prompt of the
  strategy note's §8.3. The audience is the owner, as reviewer, before `/speckit-tasks`; the depth
  is a formal gate.
- Each item asks whether the spec and plan state a requirement well, not whether any code works.
  This feature writes no RTL (FR-056); the items concern what the design document must give
  features 006 and 008. "research Rn" is a section of [research.md](../research.md);
  "data-model" is [data-model.md](../data-model.md); the "model contract" is
  [contracts/model-v3-api.md](../contracts/model-v3-api.md); the "hardware note" is
  [vhdl-genai.md](../../../research/hardware/vhdl-genai.md); FUT-GRID and FUT-HW are quoted from
  [seed-entropy-bound.md](../../../research/security/seed-entropy-bound.md) §5.1 and §5.2.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer
  evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify`
  and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
